readme:
# Glassdoor Scraper: Jobs, Salaries, Ratings & Companies

Extract job listings from [Glassdoor](https://www.glassdoor.com) across 20+ country domains. Every row carries the company's Glassdoor rating (1-5) and review count alongside title, salary, location and apply URL. Optional employer profile enrichment adds "About" text, headquarters, size range, founded year, industry, CEO, rating breakdown and open-role count for each unique company in the run.

## What it does

Runs a search on Glassdoor for one or more keyword and location pairs (or a set of pre-filtered start URLs) and returns structured rows. Three fetch modes:

1. **SERP only** (default). 25+ fields per job, sourced from Glassdoor's embedded React state plus JSON-LD.
2. **SERP + job detail** (`includeJobDetails: true`). Adds full description (plain text + HTML), direct apply URL and richer employment-type data from each job's detail page.
3. **SERP + job detail + employer profile** (`includeCompanyDetails: true`). Also resolves each unique employer to its Glassdoor company page and returns "employer-enrichment" rows with about text, HQ, size, founded year, industry, CEO, rating breakdown (culture, comp, opportunities, senior leadership, work-life balance) and a list of currently-open roles.

Uses a stealth browser stack (Firefox at the C++ level) plus residential proxy to keep Cloudflare's Bot Management happy. Warm-walks Glassdoor's homepage before touching the search URL and paginates with the real "Next" button, not by rewriting URLs.

## Pricing

Pay per result, no monthly minimum. First $5 every month is on Apify's free credit tier, so short evaluations cost nothing.

| Event | Price |
|---|---:|
| Actor start | $0.005 |
| SERP result (per job row) | $0.015 |
| Detail-page enrichment (per job, when `includeJobDetails=true`) | $0.015 |
| Employer profile (per unique employer, when `includeCompanyDetails=true`) | $0.008 |

Typical spend:
- 1,000 SERP-only jobs: ~$15.00
- 1,000 jobs with full details: ~$30.00
- 1,000 jobs with details + employer profiles (assuming ~200 unique employers): ~$31.60

Existing customers who subscribed before 2026-09-03 are grandfathered on their original rate.

## Input

The only required field is either `searchQueries` or `startUrls`.

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `searchQueries` | string[] | `["software engineer"]` | One or more keywords. Each runs separately. |
| `startUrls` | string[] | `[]` | Pre-filtered Glassdoor search URLs. Preserves any filters set in Glassdoor's UI. |
| `location` | string | empty | City, region or country text applied to every keyword. |
| `country` | enum | `us` | Which Glassdoor domain (us, uk, gb, ca, au, ie, in, de, fr, nl, es, it, br, mx, ar, sg, hk, ch, at, be). |
| `includeJobDetails` | boolean | `false` | Fetch each job's detail page for description + apply URL. |
| `includeCompanyDetails` | boolean | `false` | Resolve each unique employer's Glassdoor profile page. Auto-enables `includeJobDetails`. |
| `sortBy` | enum | `newest` | `newest` = newest first (adds `fromAge=1` filter), `relevance` = Glassdoor's default ranking. Legacy `date` still accepted. |
| `maxResults` | integer | 25 | Total cap across all queries and URLs. |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | integer | 200 | Cap per keyword or start URL. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer | 1 | Reserved; scraping is sequential today. |

## Output fields

Every job row carries these fields (nullable where noted):

- Identity: `id` (Glassdoor jobListingId), `title`, `company_name`, `company_logo_url`, `job_url`, `source_platform`
- Location: `location`, `city`, `state`, `country`
- Salary: `salary_min`, `salary_max`, `salary_currency`, `salary_period`, `salary_text`, `salary_estimated`, `salary_source`
- Job attributes: `employment_type`, `workplace_type`, `easy_apply`, `sponsored`, `apply_url`, `apply_type`
- Description: `description_snippet`, `description_full` (details mode), `description_html` (details mode)
- Timing: `posted_at` (YYYY-MM-DD, approximate day-granularity), `posted_at_datetime` (ISO-8601 with UTC time, e.g. `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`), `age_days`, `scraped_at`
- Employer signals: `company_rating` (1-5 on SERP), `review_count`, `employer_id`, `employer_profile_url`
- SERP context: `search_query`, `search_location`, `serp_page`, `extraction_mode`
- `_type`: `"job"` on every row

When `includeCompanyDetails=true`, each job row is enriched in-place with: `company_about`, `company_website`, `company_headquarters`, `company_size_range`, `company_founded_year`, `company_industry`, `company_sector`, `company_revenue_range`, `company_ceo`, `company_ceo_approval_pct`, `company_glassdoor_rating`, `company_rating_culture`, `company_rating_compensation`, `company_rating_opportunities`, `company_rating_senior_leadership`, `company_rating_work_life_balance`, `company_rating_diversity`, `company_recommend_pct`, `company_active_jobs_count`, `company_active_jobs[]`.

## Use with AI agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client (Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, custom agents).

Apify MCP server URL:

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/glassdoor-scraper
```

Example prompt once connected:

> "Use glassdoor-scraper to pull the 20 newest senior product manager jobs in London with full details and employer profiles. Return as a table with company, rating, salary range and apply URL."

## Why this scraper

- Employer rating and review count on every SERP row, not just the primary listing.
- Structured salary parsing that keeps Glassdoor's "estimated" flag and source (employer vs. Glassdoor).
- Optional employer profile pass returns 18+ company fields deduplicated per employer, useful for lead-gen and market mapping.
- 20+ country domains with the same schema.
- Bounded, retry-hardened pagination that gives up quickly on dead queries instead of billing you for empty runs.

## Use cases

- Compensation benchmarking: pull salary ranges across cities and titles.
- Recruiter lead-gen: surface companies actively hiring for a role plus their contact-adjacent employer info (HQ, size, industry, CEO).
- Market intelligence: track competitor rating trends and open-role counts over time.
- Candidate flow: dedupe Glassdoor rows into a personal or ATS pipeline.

## Notes and limits

- Glassdoor's "newest" sort is a `fromAge` filter, not a true recency sort. If you need every posting regardless of age, use `sortBy: relevance` and paginate deeper.
- Salary ranges are commonly Glassdoor estimates rather than official bands. The `salary_estimated` and `salary_source` fields tell you which is which.
- Employer profile pages sometimes omit fields (particularly for smaller companies). Nulls are preserved rather than backfilled with guesses.
- The Cloudflare warm-walk adds ~5 seconds per browser session start. Runtime scales roughly linearly with `maxResults`.
- Cost drivers: SERP page count (~30 rows per page), whether `includeJobDetails` is on, and unique employer count for the Phase H pass.
